name: LSHBOX
listed_description: A c++ toolbox of locality-sensitive hashing (LSH), provides several popular LSH algorithms, also support Python and MATLAB.
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline reachable. The README only ranks LSHBOX's own eight schemes against each other without numbers ('Double-Bit Quantization Hashing and Iterative Quantization perform very good and are superior to other schemes'); the Python and MATLAB snippets note a second query takes 'about 3s' or 'about 0.5s' without re-indexing (self versus self). The repo root (include, matlab, python, tools) has no benchmark results, the LSHBOX-sample-data README only describes the audio dataset, and a web search found no third-party comparison against FLANN, LSHKIT, linear scan or other LSH libraries. It is also a GPL-3.0 toolbox for image retrieval, not a stdlib hash-map replacement, so the guessed hash-maps-sets category does not apply.

name: m2cgen
listed_description: A CLI tool to transpile trained classic ML models into a native C code with zero dependencies.
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. The README has no performance or benchmark section (FAQ covers recursion limits, unpickling and float64 only), the repo page shows no benchmark material, and the READMEs of dmlc/treelite, siboehm/lleaves and kossisoroyce/timber do not mention m2cgen. Web searches found no benchmark of m2cgen-generated C against scikit-learn, XGBoost or LightGBM predict; one search snippet pointed to a paper that used m2cgen output (arXiv 2411.10143) but arXiv is blocked here and it was not opened. It is a code generator (a Python tool that emits C), not a faster implementation of a library facility, so no named baseline applies.

name: mbed TLS
reason: No claim or number that Mbed TLS is faster than a named baseline. The README (raw.githubusercontent.com/Mbed-TLS/mbedtls) has no performance statement and only mentions OpenSSL as a test-script peer; the project ships a benchmark program that prints absolute rates. Where comparisons exist Mbed TLS is the slower side: search snippets of a wolfSSL blog (posts.wolfssl.com, blocked here, so not opened) report wolfCrypt 15.7x faster for AES-256-GCM, 5.0x for SHA-256 and 49.3x for ECDSA P-256 verify on an i9-11950H, and another snippet says OpenSSL does a TLS handshake about 18x faster than Mbed TLS (source not opened). Speedups quoted for Mbed TLS itself (about 30 percent faster handshakes from 2.22.0 to 3.2.1, user report on the blocked trustedfirmware list) are self versus self. Mbed TLS targets small footprint, and the guessed concurrency-queues-locks category does not fit a crypto and TLS library; tls.mbed.org was not opened.

name: memory
listed_description: STL compatible C++ memory allocator library.
reason: No numeric comparison against std::allocator or any other baseline reachable. The README, doc/index.md and CHANGELOG.md contain no numbers (the changelog only says 'improved performance of pool allocators'), the repo tree has no benchmark directory (tool/ holds node_size_debugger and test_types only), and discussion #154 has the maintainer telling a user to benchmark memory_pool<array_pool> themselves. The only performance material is the author's blog series 'How I have beaten Boost.Pool' (search snippet: 'equal or faster than Boost.Pool', no numbers, baseline Boost.Pool not std::allocator); foonathan.net, www.foonathan.net and memory.foonathan.net are blocked here (EGRESS_BLOCKED), so no page with numbers was opened.

name: mill
reason: No numeric comparison against a named baseline reachable. The README is a 355-byte stub pointing to libmill.org (blocked here, EGRESS_BLOCKED). The repo perf/ directory (ctxswitch.c, go.c, chan.c, chr.c, chs.c, c10k.c, whispers.c) only prints absolute rates for libmill itself, with no Go, pthread or other library in the code, and the author's stable-release gist has design goals but no numbers. A search snippet of libmill.org quotes up to 20 million coroutines and 50 million context switches per second, an absolute figure without a baseline (the snippet's 'faster than goroutines' framing is the search tool's inference, not a project claim). The guessed concurrency-queues-locks category is also wrong: libmill is a coroutine and channel library.
